# Dr. ***Stephanie Miles-Richardson***, DVM, PhD

*Founding Chair & Professor*  
**Department of Public Health Education**  
Morehouse School of Medicine — Atlanta, Georgia

---

Dr. Stephanie Miles-Richardson is a **national leader in environmental health, climate justice, and public health education**. She serves as the ***Founding Chair*** of the Department of Public Health Education at Morehouse School of Medicine (MSM), while also holding the roles of **Associate Dean of Graduate Education in Public Health** and **Director of the Master of Public Health Program**. 

Prior to joining MSM in 2008, Dr. Miles-Richardson completed over a decade of **federal public health service**, including roles as a **United States Public Health Service Commissioned Officer** and **Scientific Technical Advisor** for a $4 million toxicology research program at the Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry. She later served as **Associate Director of Minority Health and Health Disparities Policy** at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). 

Dr. Miles-Richardson has also made **historic contributions to the governance of academic public health**. She was appointed to the **Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH)** in 2015 and later became **the first African American to serve as President** of both:
- the *Association of Accredited Public Health Programs* (2018), and
- **CEPH** (2019). 

Her national influence extends to leadership in **One Health**, **health disparities policy**, and **climate-focused public health curriculum**. She received grant support from the **Association for Prevention Teaching and Research** and CDC to develop an interdisciplinary **Climate Justice** course for wide dissemination. She was also awarded an **honorary diploma by the American Veterinary Epidemiology Society** for her impact in advancing human and animal health. 

Currently, she serves as the **inaugural Director of the Beacon of Hope Center of Excellence on Climate and Environmental Health** at MSM and as a **Governing Councilor** for the **Environment Section of the American Public Health Association**.
